tasks.title: Mask ephemeral e2e credentials and suppress diagnostics after persistent collection failure
tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, complete Behavior, Docs and Tests sections; Required behavior items 1-7; Decisions (including persistent fail-closed invalidation); all Counterexamples; Acceptance (deploy) items 1-10; Performance impact and Security impact. Implement one run-owned credential registry across shared console helpers, standalone setup and runtime form collection; consume it with literal masking and S1-S5 fallback suppression in compose cleanup, failed or invalid-registry child replay and the CI dev diagnostic script. A failed append persistently invalidates the registry across processes; helpers never recreate it, every diagnostic consumer suppresses log lines, and both run owners turn an otherwise successful exit into failure. Preserve scenario requests/checks/success output and raw security scans on valid runs. Implement all 33 redaction cases (32 when root skips L7) and the existing seven setup cases, update README.md and dev/README.md in the same change, and restrict ci.yml to the specified dev wiring. Keep docs/cli.md and all protected paths unchanged. Collection, registry trust and lifetime, consumers and regression form one coupled mechanism.

acceptance.expected: Before any implementation edit, record this full SHA as BASE in the PR evidence and export BASE for subsequent checks. Use the actual implementation base, not a later merge-base or the plan's inspected SHA. Prepare disposable baseline and red-proof worktrees outside the implementation checkout; keep an unchanged baseline worktree BASE_DIR for controls and timing. No target .factory, plan, evidence or scope-checker file is committed.

Run these controls rather than relying on previous spec-run evidence. Preserve the five original redaction cases' names, sentinels and assertions in the candidate.

Run on the unchanged recorded base and require exit 0 when docker compose config is available. If that prerequisite is missing, name it for the base and candidate separately and do not call either run green.

RED_BASE_DIR is a disposable worktree at recorded BASE with only the candidate e2e/redact.test.sh copied over using file tools; production stays unchanged. Run all 33 cases even after failures (32 with the L7 root skip). K1-K5 each print FAIL: <category>: ...printed the credential: five independent leak failures, not a missing helper, syntax error or stub failure. F1-F5 fail for missing suppression. E1-E5, C1-C3 and V1 pass. R1, C4, L2, L3, L5-L8, P1 and W1-W3 fail for missing interfaces (except skipped L7 as root), and are excluded from the leak proof. Exit 1; record every result and exact counts. Absent collect_needles/replay_redacted/setup_exit extraction yields empty eval, allowing K1-K5 to execute on the base. Remove this disposable worktree after recording evidence.

Exit 0 and exactly 'redact.test: 33 cases passed'; every case reports ok. As root, exactly 'skip: L7 (root ignores file modes)' and 'redact.test: 32 cases passed'. Implement every assertion of Repository: deploy Tests E1-E5, K1-K5, R1, F1-F5, V1, C1-C4, L1-L8, P1 and W1-W3. K1-K5 collect only through real helpers in child Bash processes, delete response/jar files before actual compose cleanup, mask all category sentinels in unlabelled stub logs and retain the neighbouring plain line. Cover two rotated jar and Set-Cookie values, successive CSRF values, selected/decoy/runtime form tokens, two generated TOTP values and response-only recovery codes (all ten retained; first and tenth in logs). req stdout is exactly 200. R1 proves registry contents, mode 600 and the 5/6-character boundary. F1-F5 prove unrecorded shape suppression; V1 preserves all five ordinary counterexamples including seven-digit code and UUID shapes. C1-C4 cover Authorization, SMTP, status/notify files and probe secrets. L1-L4 prove early failure exit 1, missing/unreadable needles fail closed and registry-directory removal. L5 records A through csrf in one child, fails recording B through csrf in a second child with trap '' XFSZ and ulimit -f 0 (output to a pipe), then tries C through needle_add in a third child without the limit. The append fails while the registry remains readable before invalidation; step 2 exits 1 with 'FAIL: needle registry: append failed' and no B. Step 3 returns 1, the registry stays absent and its .invalid marker exists; needles_valid fails in a fourth child. Actual compose cleanup with incoming exit 0 exits 1, prints 'FAIL: needle registry: collection failed; diagnostics suppressed' and '[redacted: no needles file]', no plain line or A/B/C, and removes the registry directory. L6 proves a marker alone invalidates a readable complete registry: cleanup with incoming 0 exits 1 and suppresses D/plain line; replay_redacted prints only the fail-closed marker. L7 proves mode 400 rejects validity and append (root skip only). L8 extracts the real setup_exit: valid registry plus incoming 0 exits 0 and removes work; invalid registry plus incoming 0 exits 1 with the collection-failed message and removes work; incoming 1 stays 1. P1 masks recorded and suppresses labelled child output while retaining plain lines. W1 exits 0 with ps/plain line visible and the sentinel masked; W2 missing registry exits 1 with ps/marker only and no-argument usage exits 2; W3 invalidated by the L5 append failure exits 1 with ps, marker and collection-failed message, no sentinel/plain line. No actual credentials in fixtures.

Exit 0 and exactly 'console-setup.test: 7 cases passed'. Keep A-G names, literal stdout, request/form-token checks, the F failure check and stdout/stderr credential scan. A/B/C/E/G use a private registry (directory 700, file 600); independent stub state proves all issued CSRF and form tokens, every TOTP code, all ten recovery codes, owner password and setup key are recorded when applicable. D/F leave E2E_NEEDLES unset and preserve original checks. form() records issued CSRF values in its independent state file. No recording output changes success text. Expected values come from independent stub state and fixtures, never the registry. After each applicable case the file is mode 600 and no E2E_NEEDLES.invalid marker exists.

acceptance.command: git diff "$BASE" HEAD -- e2e/console-lib.sh e2e/console-setup.sh e2e/runtime-settings.sh e2e/redact.sh e2e/compose-e2e.sh e2e/failure-logs.sh
acceptance.expected: Security checklist and compatibility inspection confirms Required behavior 1-6 and the Decisions exactly. needles_valid is silent and accepts empty E2E_NEEDLES; otherwise it requires no .invalid marker, a regular non-symlink readable/writable registry and a writable parent directory. Only the run owner creates the mode 600 registry in a mode 700 directory. needle_add is silent, ignores values shorter than 6, refuses invalid registries before appending, uses umask 077, and on append failure calls needles_invalidate then returns 1. Invalidation silently best-effort creates a mode 600 .invalid marker and removes the registry, returns 0, and never allows helper resurrection. Every recording point has the value-free 'needle registry: append failed' failure. All jar cookies (including HttpOnly), case-insensitive Set-Cookie values, all response CSRF/form values and recovery codes are recorded before overwrite. req preserves curl status/stdout even on failure; totp_after records skipped codes too; selected helpers, owner setup and runtime fields record as specified. Literal values are never evaluated or treated as regexes. compose overrides inherited E2E_NEEDLES, creates private state immediately after its trap, includes probe secrets, masks child output when failed OR registry invalid, and preserves raw scans/order. cleanup and setup_exit promote incoming 0 to 1 when invalid with 'FAIL: needle registry: collection failed; diagnostics suppressed'; existing failure codes stay unchanged. Invalid registry makes redact_needles remove its output and return 1; cleanup, replay_redacted and failure-logs then print only '[redacted: no needles file]' instead of any log line. Registry/marker/directory are removed after the last compose consumer on success, failure and invalidation; setup_exit removes its own work without deleting the CI-owned registry. failure-logs validates arguments (exit 2), prints ps before redacted logs, cleans temporary needles, and exits 1 with the collection-failed message when invalid, otherwise 0. Scenario requests, selection, assertions, valid-run success/skip text, raw scans/order/messages, teardown order and original failure status stay unchanged except the specified invalid-registry failure. No service behavior, logger, auth flow, setup-code collection, action/package dependency, pin or Compose change.

Both required docs change in the same implementation. README e2e paragraph names admin/service tokens, owner password/key, secret files, probe secrets and the five recorded categories, E2E_NEEDLES private registry, [redacted], [suppressed: credential line], missing-or-invalid-registry marker and the e2e-only boundary. It explains that recording failure invalidates the registry for the rest of the run and fails the run even if all steps passed. State the Decisions residual limit: inability both to remove the registry and to create its marker while the registry and its directory still appear writable cannot be detected; no scenario path produces it. README CI dev paragraph names bash e2e/failure-logs.sh dev/compose.yaml with the same masking and fail-closed rule. dev/README explains mode 600 E2E_NEEDLES collection, failure on collection error, and the masked stack diagnostic command that prints no log line when invalid. No added sentinel quote or credential-extraction recipe; ordinary operator documentation in docs/cli.md remains protected.

With sibling service checkouts, Docker/Compose and free ports 3000, 8080 and 8082, exit 0 with ==> All checks passed and the required dev ok lines, preserving scenario checks/success output. Run every check of the touched dev job as well (init-secrets, dev build/start, wait-ready, console setup, diagnostic failure wiring, teardown, CLI dependency install and source CLI stack.sh dev); W1-W3 exercise its failure command with stubs. If prerequisites are absent name them exactly. PR CI dev and e2e-dev jobs must pass; unit/stub tests alone do not establish live-stack success. Do not run the Docker bench (#834).

acceptance.command:
python3 -c 'import pathlib, subprocess, tempfile
allowed = ["e2e/console-lib.sh","e2e/console-setup.sh","e2e/runtime-settings.sh","e2e/redact.sh","e2e/compose-e2e.sh","e2e/failure-logs.sh","e2e/redact.test.sh","e2e/console-setup.test.sh",".github/workflows/ci.yml","README.md","dev/README.md"]
protected = ["AGENTS.md","CLAUDE.md","package.json","bun.lock","bunfig.toml","biome.json","tsconfig.json","eslint.config.js","lefthook.yml","common","minimal","full","demo","dev/compose.yaml","e2e/compose.e2e.yaml","e2e/compose.runtime.yaml","e2e/compose.subscriptions.yaml","e2e/console-probes.sh","e2e/console-incidents.sh","e2e/subscriptions.sh","e2e/runtime-settings.test.sh","e2e/totp.mjs","docs","scripts","cli",".github/workflows/release.yml"]
def git(repo, *args):
    return subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], text=True)
tracked_protected = subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-files", "--", *protected], text=True).splitlines()
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="870-scope-") as directory:
    repo = pathlib.Path(directory)
    git(repo, "init", "-q")
    def write(path, value):
        target = repo / path
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target.write_text(value)
    for path in sorted(set(allowed + tracked_protected)):
        write(path, "base\n")
    def commit():
        git(repo, "-c", "user.name=scope fixture", "-c", "user.email=scope@example.invalid", "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit", "-qm", "fixture")
    git(repo, "add", ".")
    commit()
    base = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
    def checks(expected):
        changed = git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", base, "HEAD").splitlines()
        return {
            "allowlist": sorted(changed) == sorted(expected),
            "index": git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", "--cached") == "",
            "worktree": git(repo, "diff", "--name-only") == "",
            "status": git(repo, "status", "--porcelain") == "",
            "protected": subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "diff", "--quiet", base, "HEAD", "--", *protected]).returncode == 0,
        }
    def reset():
        git(repo, "reset", "--hard", base)
    assert all(checks([]).values())
    for path in allowed:
        write(path, "allowed\n")
    git(repo, "add", "--", *allowed)
    commit()
    assert all(checks(allowed).values())
    reset()
    write("AGENTS.md", "protected\n")
    result = checks([])
    assert not result["worktree"] and not result["status"]
    reset()
    write("AGENTS.md", "protected\n")
    git(repo, "add", "AGENTS.md")
    result = checks([])
    assert not result["index"] and not result["status"]
    reset()
    write("AGENTS.md", "protected\n")
    git(repo, "add", "AGENTS.md")
    commit()
    result = checks([])
    assert result["index"] and result["worktree"] and result["status"]
    assert not result["allowlist"] and not result["protected"]
    reset()
    write("AGENTS.md", "protected\n")
    git(repo, "add", "AGENTS.md")
    write("AGENTS.md", "base\n")
    assert git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", base) == ""
    result = checks([])
    assert not result["index"] and not result["worktree"] and not result["status"]
    reset()
    write("AGENTS.md", "protected\n")
    git(repo, "add", "AGENTS.md")
    commit()
    write("AGENTS.md", "base\n")
    assert git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", base) == ""
    result = checks([])
    assert not result["allowlist"] and not result["protected"] and not result["worktree"] and not result["status"]
print("ok: 7 scope fixture states; fixture removed")
'
acceptance.expected: Exit 0 and 'ok: 7 scope fixture states; fixture removed'. Use the exact task allowlist and protected list outside the checkout. Clean control and allowed committed changes pass; unstaged, staged, cleanly committed protected changes and both restored-worktree variants fail the relevant independent checks. Both restored variants show an empty base-to-worktree diff while index/commit/allowlist checks expose the unauthorized change. Remove the fixture afterwards.

Public diff adds no real credential; only synthetic sentinel values inside e2e/*.test.sh. PR text contains categories only, no extraction recipe. PR evidence records full BASE, independent baseline control results, all 33 branch cases (32 plus the L7 skip as root), five category leak failures on base with exact counts, registry permissions/lifetime, suppression and persistent fail-closed behavior (L5-L8/W3, cross-process no resurrection, incoming-success failure status and eventual cleanup), residual limit, compatibility/security review, mawk result, CI diff restrictions, full required-check results, live-stack/CI outcomes or precise missing prerequisites, all interleaved CPU samples/means/deltas, and the seven-state scope fixture and separate committed/index/worktree/status/protected checks. Do not claim a service emits credentials based on stub evidence. Remove disposable worktrees and evidence from the checkout before handoff.
